Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a well-defined cavitary lesion in the right upper lung zone containing a rounded soft-tissue mass separated from the cavity wall by a crescent of air (air crescent sign), which is the classic radiographic appearance of an aspergilloma (fungus ball). This finding is distinct from pneumothorax, pleural effusion, or mediastinal shift, none of which are primarily depicted here.
